concepts.quote: for (int i = 1; i < x.length; i++) x[i] = x[i - 1];
concepts.why: The new loop goes upward and copies forward, so it overwrites each value before it is read and fills the array with x[0] instead of undoing the shift.
To undo the shift each element must move left (x[i-1] = x[i]) and the old first element must be saved and put back at the end; keeping the original x[i] = x[i-1] cannot reverse it.
The answer uses i++ correctly as the stand-alone loop update that adds 1, but gives no reasoning about it.
The header correctly has an initializer, a condition and an update, but the answer doesn't trace or relate the loop.
